verdict.reasoning: Patient reports cough starting "like five days ago" and clarifies it is "quite dry" and "I'm coughing maybe every twenty, thirty minutes or so" with "my nose is just constantly streaming."
When asked about blood from nose, patient states "No, it's pretty green," indicating green nasal discharge and denial of epistaxis.

Patient denies chest pain ("Any chest pain?" "No"), denies difficulty breathing or pain on deep breath ("No, that's all fine"), and denies coughing up blood ("Have you coughed up any blood..." "Nope").
Patient reports "I've been feeling really hot... sometimes I'm feeling really chilly, needing to be under a blanket" and confirms "no" when asked if temperature has been checked with a thermometer.
Doctor asks "Any headaches or change in your vision?" and patient replies "No," then adds "I've had quite achy muscles," consistent with myalgias without headache or vision change.

Patient reports "I had some diarrhoea" at onset which "since then it's all been pretty fine" and later denies current vomiting or diarrhoea ("No vomiting, diarrhoea now?" "No"). Eating and drinking are okay. Nausea was never mentioned; stating she denies nausea adds information not in transcript.

Doctor asks about passing water and increased frequency/thirst: "And passing water OK?" "Yeah, that's fine." and "Any increase in frequency... or any increased thirst?" "No, not particularly," supporting normal urination without polyuria or polydipsia.

Patient states "normally, do you have any chest problems?" "Uh, no" and clarifies wheeze only with intense exercise: "if I do intense exercise, then yes. But not..." and denies regular chest infections: "do you regularly have any infections in your chest..." "No."
Early in consult patient states "I'm diabetic," and later confirms medical problems as "just the hypertension and the diabetes."
Patient says "I've got hypertension" and repeats "just the hypertension and the diabetes."
When asked about drugs, patient states "I think something called metformin."
Patient reports "lisinopril I think is the other one" and when asked dose replies "two hundred," matching the claim.

Patient says they are using "quite a few lemon sips" and clarifies "maybe two or three. Maybe, like, at the start of the day and at the end of the day," adding that it "tends to soothe my throat a bit."
When asked "Any allergies to any medications at all?" patient replies "Not that I'm aware of, no," consistent with no known drug allergies.
Patient notes "I sometimes suffer from some, like, hay fever. But, um, but it's not bad," consistent with intermittent seasonal allergic rhinitis.
Patient states living with "my partner and my dog" and answers employment as "Yes. I'm an office manager."
When asked about alcohol, patient responds "Yes, the odd cherry," indicating occasional alcohol consumption.

Transcript documents 5 days of dry cough and "nose is just constantly streaming" with green discharge and subjective fevers/chills; doctor describes it as an infection likely viral ("most of the time, these infections are caused by viruses, so they do normally settle by themselves"). No red flags are present as patient denies SOB, chest pain, and hemoptysis.

Patient is diabetic and when asked "Do you have blood sugar checking equipment? Do you check?" replies "No," indicating no self-monitoring. She reports a blood test about three weeks ago: "Yeah, it was normal. It was around three weeks ago."
Patient has hypertension and says BP was checked "a while ago" and cannot recall stability ("I can't remember"), matching unclear control status.
Doctor advises "It's fine to carry on what you're doing at the moment, with the lemsip. I wouldn't take... that contains paracetamol so don't take any other paracetamol containing products."

While hydration is implicitly relevant, the doctor only confirms "you're drinking well, holding down fluids OK?" and does not explicitly instruct to maintain or increase hydration as part of the plan.

Doctor states "the cough syrup isn't advisable in the daytime... But if you're kept up all night and you can't sleep at all, then it's OK to have a little bit of cough syrup, just to settle that down."
Doctor emphasizes "it's definitely worth getting a thermometer and checking your temperature" and patient asks about obtaining one from a pharmacy, confirming this as part of monitoring.

Doctor advises re-contact if "the temperature's ongoing, above thirty seven point five, thirty eight" or if "your cough's getting worse, you're coughing up lots of nasty phlegm or you cough up any blood or get blood coming out your nose, or any shortness of breath, chest pain."

Discussion includes "With the diabetes you are a bit more likely to get a bacterial infection" and patient says "So, then we would at potentially antibiotics at that time, perhaps?" Doctor answers "Yeah, potentially. If it is, if it's not settling or the temperature's ongoing, getting worse, then we definitely need to talk to you again," implying consideration of antibiotics if not improving.
Doctor instructs "make sure that you have the regular diabetes and blood pressure checkups that your GP has asked you for," indicating routine GP follow-up.
